voiceover: Twenty twenty. <break time="500ms"/> A dip across the board. Every product appears to get cheaper overnight. But this isn't because food prices dropped. During COVID, lower-wage workers disproportionately lost their jobs — retail, hospitality, food service. The people who remained employed skewed higher-income. So the median wage jumped. Not because anyone got a raise. Because the composition of who was still working changed. <break time="500ms"/> The prices on the chart were real. The wage improvement was a statistical artifact.

visual.description: Race chart continues into 2020. Chapter marker: 'ACT 3: THE RECKONING' fades in (Montserrat Bold 36px). All 6 lines dip downward at 2020 — a dramatic synchronized drop. COVID annotation callout: a bordered card overlaid on the chart at 2020 with text 'COVID Wage Anomaly: Median jumped as lower-wage workers lost jobs. Not a real improvement.' Card uses surface background, Accent Cream text, Inter 16px. Red exclamation icon. The dip is visually striking — from various 2019 positions, all lines drop ~10-15% simultaneously.

notes: The COVID dip is one of the most deceptive moments in the data. The annotation card is ESSENTIAL — without it, viewers might think food actually got cheaper during COVID. The card should appear 2 seconds after the dip becomes visible, with a subtle bounce entrance (spring stiffness 80, damping 18). The warning icon should be in Muted Red. All 6 lines dropping simultaneously is visually dramatic — animate them dropping over 15 frames.
